title: Pawn majorities

D0.outcome: Explains that a majority of pawns on one wing can create a passed pawn, and that the 'candidate' pawn leads.

D1.outcome: In a pawn-ending skeleton, states which pawn should advance first and shows how the passed pawn arises.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled pawn endings, decides whether a majority wins or draws and chooses the first pawn move (the candidate, not the middle pawn).

D3.outcome: Verifies with counting and opposition, and sees when king position or tempo makes the numbers irrelevant.

conditions: A healthy, uncompromised majority with no tactical interference.
When all pawns are on one wing, exchanges alone do not create a passer and the opposition matters.
contrasts: Pushing the middle pawn first lets the opponent fix the majority.
The majority is not converted because tempo and king position favour the defender.
Equal pawn counts on the wing.
